R code for: Miller, E. J., Steward, B. A., Witkower, Z., Sutherland, C. A. M., Krumhuber, E. G., & Dawel, A. (2023). AI hyper-realism: Why AI faces are perceived as More real than human ones. *Psychological Science.*
Contact details: amy.dawel@anu.edu.au

The analyses herein are for Miller et al.'s (2023) Experiment 1 - replication & confidence extension of Nightingale, S. J., & Farid, H. (2022). AI-synthesized faces are indistinguishable from real faces and more trustworthy. *Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 119*(8), e2120481119.

# Load R packages

Here, we load the required R packages.

```{r, setup, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE}

#clear workspace
rm(list = ls())

#list packages 
lib <- (c("rmarkdown", #RStudio markdown
          "knitr", #generating RStudio output
          "readr", #read in data
          "kableExtra", #extra tools for styling kable tables in R markdown knit
          "tidyverse", #also loads ggplot2, dplyr, tidyr, readr, purrr, tibble
          "Hmisc", #miscellaneous          
          "psych", #core psychology functions e.g. ANOVA
          "psycho", #for signal detection analyses
          "apaTables", #for APA table output
          "lme4", #linear modelling
          "rstatix", #for checking outliers
          "ggpubr", #for publishable plots
          "ggpmisc", #stat_fit_glance function
          "pander" #for outputing correlation matrices
          ))

#load packages
for (i in 1:length(lib)){
  pkg <- lib[i]
library(pkg, character.only = TRUE)
}

#turn off scientific notation
#options(scipen = 999)

#set date for file saving
dt <- Sys.Date()

```

# Load & organise datasets

Here, we load the datasets for male and female participants separately, from Miller et al.'s replication of Nightingale & Farid (2022) Expt 1.

Variable labels are generally formatted as follows:

-   Letter 1 = real or synthetic (r or s)

-   Letter 2 = black or east asian or south asian or white (b or e or s or w)

-   Letter 3 = male or female (m or f) 

-   Number = stimulus number from 1-50

-   Suffix .acc or .conf = CG/human accuracy or confidence rating

```{r, load-data}

#import raw data separately from male and female participants
df.malePs <- read.csv("../data/LM_Expt1_malePs.csv", na.strings = "")
df.malePs <- as.data.frame(df.malePs)
df.malePs$ProlificGender <- "Male"
df.femalePs <- read.csv("../data/LM_Expt1_femalePs.csv", na.strings = "")
df.femalePs <- as.data.frame(df.femalePs)
df.femalePs$ProlificGender <- "Female"

```

Here, we bind the male and female participant data together and set-up the data for further analyses.

```{r, data-wrangling}

#bind female and male data together 
df.allPs <- rbind(df.femalePs, df.malePs)

#remove cases that never started study
df.allPs <- filter(df.allPs, !is.na(prolificId))

#remove superfluous variables
df.allPs <- select(df.allPs, -contains(c("firstclick", "lastclick", "clickcount", "prac")))

#code condition participants were assigned to
df.allPs <- df.allPs %>% 
  mutate(across(matches("cond"), ~recode(.x,"FL_106" = "mc1",
                                         "FL_107" = "mc2", 
                                         "FL_108" = "fc1", 
                                         "FL_109" = "fc2" ))) #conditions are: mc1 = male faces, CG response button left, mc2 = male faces, CG response button right, fc1 = female faces, CG response button left, fc2 = female faces, CG response button right

#select columns with participant info for matching later
partinfo <- select(df.allPs, contains(c("Duration", "age", "gender", "liveInUS", "yearsOutside", "state", "confirmWhite", "exclusion", "attentionCheck", "decisionQ", "overallConfidence", "ResponseId", "progress", "operateSys", "resolution", "InfoUsed", "prolific", "StartDate", "incNoCond", "ProlificGender")) & -contains("Language"))

#select variables needed for analysis + id for matching later
df.allPs <- select(df.allPs, ends_with(c("ResponseId", "cond", "mc1", "mc2", "fc1", "fc2")))

#separate data by conditions #NB. This also removes rows for people who opened experiment but did not start it, i.e., were never assigned to a condition.
mc1 <- select(df.allPs, "ResponseId", "cond", ends_with(c(".mc1"))) %>%
  filter(cond == "mc1")
mc2 <- select(df.allPs, "ResponseId", "cond", ends_with(c(".mc2"))) %>%
  filter(cond == "mc2")
fc1 <- select(df.allPs, "ResponseId", "cond", ends_with(c(".fc1"))) %>%
  filter(cond == "fc1")
fc2 <- select(df.allPs, "ResponseId", "cond", ends_with(c(".fc2"))) %>%
  filter(cond == "fc2")

#drop condition names from column headers
colnames(mc1) <- gsub(".mc1", "", colnames(mc1))
colnames(mc2) <- gsub(".mc2", "", colnames(mc2))
colnames(fc1) <- gsub(".fc1", "", colnames(fc1))
colnames(fc2) <- gsub(".fc2", "", colnames(fc2))

#recombine data with participant info
df.allPs <- bind_rows(mc1, mc2, fc1, fc2)
df.allPs <- full_join(partinfo, df.allPs, by = NULL)

#convert to tibble
df.allPs <- as_tibble(df.allPs)

#cleanup: remove dfs that are no longer needed
rm(df.malePs, df.femalePs, partinfo, mc1, mc2, fc1, fc2)

```

# Recode data

Here, we recode participant CG/human accuracy responses so that 1 = correct and 0 = incorrect.

```{r, recode-data}

#recode experimental trials
df.allPs <- df.allPs %>% 
  mutate(across(starts_with("rw") & ends_with(".acc"), ~recode(.x,"${lm://Field/5}" = 0, "${lm://Field/6}" = 1))) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("sw") & ends_with(".acc"), ~recode(.x,"${lm://Field/5}" = 1, "${lm://Field/6}" = 0)))

#recode catch trials
df.allPs <- df.allPs %>% 
  mutate(across(contains("under50") & ends_with(".acc"), ~recode(.x,"${lm://Field/5}" = 0, "${lm://Field/6}" = 1))) %>% 
  mutate(across(contains("over50") & ends_with(".acc"), ~recode(.x,"${lm://Field/5}" = 1, "${lm://Field/6}" = 0)))

```

# Data corrections

Here, we correct responses where participants messaged via Prolific that they had made a mistake or experienced problems with the experiment. The chunk provides each participant message in full and if/how their data was managed.

```{r, data-corrections}

#ResponseId: R_3ffcAXXZMQX2kzZ
#Hello I am not sure how much it matters in for the survey I just took for you but there was one face that was obviously older than 50 but I clicked the wrong option. To make up for this I rated my confidence as zero. Intuitively I would have thought the older option would be on the right so I clicked the option on the right which was "under 50". There was no option to go back to change your answer and if you click it auto advances so mis-clicks cannot be fixed as far as I could tell.

#relevant trial recoded
df.allPs$catch4m.over50.acc[df.allPs$ResponseId == "R_3ffcAXXZMQX2kzZ"] <- 1
df.allPs$catch4m.over50.conf[df.allPs$ResponseId == "R_3ffcAXXZMQX2kzZ"] <- 100

#ResponseId: R_3FJxZ5SxmyEZ5Dr
#I messed up an image; there was an old woman and it asked if she was under or over 50. I thought I clicked the 'over 50' but I was right in the middle of the two buttons, and it clicked the left (under 50) and because you decided to abuse us workers [common behavior by educational institutions] by making it auto-advance after selection of an option (causing this page to open after EVERY single selection -  I was not able to correct it therefore, I put 0% confidence that I chose the correct option

#relevant trial recoded 
df.allPs$catch4f.over50.acc[df.allPs$ResponseId == "R_3FJxZ5SxmyEZ5Dr"] <- 1
df.allPs$catch4f.over50.conf[df.allPs$ResponseId == "R_3FJxZ5SxmyEZ5Dr"] <- 100

#ResponseId: R_2pPrgfsTC2I5GhS
#Hello! I completed this survey but the last 5 or so minutes I keep having an issue with it being able to connect to your surveys. I was able to finish/they were connecting again but they were very slow to do so, which took longer than it said it would do. Just thought I'd let you know about the server message/being disconnected here and there but only the last few minutes, so hopefully it's not an ongoing thing for you.
  
#Participant data is complete with no missing responses. No corrections required. 
  
#ResponseId: R_21ijIOsQJoDIiBp
#Hi there. I just completed your study. In the beginning, before starting, it told me that I'd occasionally be asked whether a face appeared to be 50 years of age or so, but that prompt never came up even once. Just letting you know, in case there is an error there.
  
#No error; participant performed poorly on catch trials (accuracy 2/5) and was therefore excluded based on data exclusion criteria. 

#ResponseId: R_1LjsyHjBrTnn6CG
#Hello, At about the half way mark I began running into some technical issues. Occasionally the pages would time out or I'd see the question about human/AI before the photo itself showed up.

#Participant excluded. See data-included chunk.

```

# Data screening

Here, we take a look at the distribution of RTs for CG/human trials and delete CG/human accuracy responses for individual participant trials with RTs <300 ms, indicative of pre-emptive responses.

NB. We did not analyse RTs because the experiment was administered using Qualtrics on participants own hardware and therefore factors other than participant performance may have contributed to RTs (e.g., internet speed).

```{r, screen-RTs, message=FALSE, warning = FALSE}

#reshape into wide data for RT distribution plot
df.allPs.RTs <- df.allPs %>%
  select(!starts_with("catch") & ends_with(".submitacc")) %>%
  gather("var", "RTs", convert = TRUE)

#distribution plot
ggplot(df.allPs.RTs) +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = RTs)) + 
  scale_y_continuous(expand=expansion(mult=c(0,.1))) +
  xlim(0, 1) + #adjust xlim to zoom in on an RT range
  theme_bw()

#count RTs <500ms for CG/human responses, recalling that rwm = real white male, swm = synthetic (CG) white male, rwf = real white female, swf = synthetic (CG) white female
df.allPs <- df.allPs %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(RT.Nlow = sum(c_across(!starts_with("catch") & ends_with(".submitacc")) < 0.3, na.rm = TRUE)) #this variable used to report trials excluded due to pre-emptive responding

#recode pre-emptive CG/human responses as missing 

#Thanks to Edward Carney on Stackoverflow for the following code, which was edited from their reply: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48600340/change-column-value-to-na-based-on-other-column-condition

#identify relevant columns
acc.cols <- grep(".acc", fixed = TRUE, names(df.allPs)) #NB. fixed forces exact match; otherwise pulls both .acc & .submitacc
rt.cols <- grep(".submitacc", names(df.allPs))

#for each rt column with response <300 ms, delete the corresponding .acc response (i.e., make missing)   
for (i in 1:length(rt.cols)) {
  #get indexes of < 500ms entries in .rt cols
  rt.index <- df.allPs[,rt.cols[i]] < 0.3
  #change the corresponding entries in .acc cols
  df.allPs[,acc.cols[i]][rt.index] = NA 
  df.allPs[,rt.cols[i]][rt.index] = NA
}

#sum correct catch trials
df.allPs <- df.allPs %>%
  rowwise() %>%
    mutate(catch.acc = rowSums(across(contains("catch") & ends_with(".acc")), na.rm = TRUE))

#cleanup: remove dfs that are no longer needed
rm(df.allPs.RTs, rt.index)

```

Here, we compute total missing data for CG/human accuracy and confidence ratings.

```{r, missing-data}

#compute missing data
df.allPs <- df.allPs %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  #compute N CG/human trials missing for each face type, recalling that rwm = real white male, swm = synthetic (CG) white male, rwf = real white female, swf = synthetic (CG) white female
    mutate(rwm.acc.miss = rowSums(is.na(across(starts_with("rwm0") & ends_with(".acc"))))) %>%
    mutate(rwm.acc.miss = case_when(str_detect(cond, "mc") ~ rwm.acc.miss, str_detect(cond, "fc") ~ NA_real_)) %>%
    mutate(swm.acc.miss = rowSums(is.na(across(starts_with("swm0") & ends_with(".acc"))))) %>%
    mutate(swm.acc.miss = case_when(str_detect(cond, "mc") ~ swm.acc.miss, str_detect(cond, "fc") ~ NA_real_)) %>%
    mutate(rwf.acc.miss = rowSums(is.na(across(starts_with("rwf0") & ends_with(".acc"))))) %>%
    mutate(rwf.acc.miss = case_when(str_detect(cond, "fc") ~ rwf.acc.miss, str_detect(cond, "mc") ~ NA_real_)) %>%
    mutate(swf.acc.miss = rowSums(is.na(across(starts_with("swf0") & ends_with(".acc"))))) %>%
    mutate(swf.acc.miss = case_when(str_detect(cond, "fc") ~ swf.acc.miss, str_detect(cond, "mc") ~ NA_real_)) %>%
  #compute N confidence ratings missing for each face type
    mutate(rwm.conf.miss = rowSums(is.na(across(starts_with("rwm0") & ends_with(".conf"))))) %>%
    mutate(rwm.conf.miss = case_when(str_detect(cond, "mc") ~ rwm.conf.miss, str_detect(cond, "fc") ~ NA_real_)) %>%
    mutate(swm.conf.miss = rowSums(is.na(across(starts_with("swm0") & ends_with(".conf"))))) %>%
    mutate(swm.conf.miss = case_when(str_detect(cond, "mc") ~ swm.conf.miss, str_detect(cond, "fc") ~ NA_real_)) %>%
    mutate(rwf.conf.miss = rowSums(is.na(across(starts_with("rwf0") & ends_with(".conf"))))) %>%
    mutate(rwf.conf.miss = case_when(str_detect(cond, "fc") ~ rwf.conf.miss, str_detect(cond, "mc") ~ NA_real_)) %>%
    mutate(swf.conf.miss = rowSums(is.na(across(starts_with("swf0") & ends_with(".conf"))))) %>%
    mutate(swf.conf.miss = case_when(str_detect(cond, "fc") ~ swf.conf.miss, str_detect(cond, "mc") ~ NA_real_))

#combine N missing into single variable for each type of face (human or CG)
df.allPs$rw.acc.miss <- coalesce(df.allPs$rwm.acc.miss, df.allPs$rwf.acc.miss)
df.allPs$sw.acc.miss <- coalesce(df.allPs$swm.acc.miss, df.allPs$swf.acc.miss)
df.allPs$rw.conf.miss <- coalesce(df.allPs$rwm.conf.miss, df.allPs$rwf.conf.miss)
df.allPs$sw.conf.miss <- coalesce(df.allPs$swm.conf.miss, df.allPs$swf.conf.miss)

```

# Select included sample

Here, we screen the sample to select participants who meet inclusion/exclusion criteria and also code the reasons for participant exclusions.

```{r, data-included}

#identify cases to exclude
df.allPs <- df.allPs %>%
  rowwise() %>%
      mutate(exclude = case_when(
        ResponseId == "R_1LjsyHjBrTnn6CG" ~ "exclude", #participant reported technical difficulties; see data-corrections chunk
        Progress < 98 ~ "exclude", #exclude if <98% complete
        str_detect(operateSys, "Android") ~ "exclude", #exclude if used phone
        operateSys == "iPhone" ~ "exclude", #exclude if used phone
        confirmWhite != "Yes, my ethnicity is White/European/Caucasian" ~ "exclude", #exclude if not White
        USstate == "I do not reside in the United States" ~ "exclude", #exclude if not resident in US
        yearsOutsideUS > 2 ~ "exclude", #exclude if >2 years outside US prior to 18
        incNoCond != "No, none of these statements apply to me" ~ "exclude", #exclude if reported condition likely to affect face processing
        catch.acc < 4 ~ "exclude", #exclude if more than 1 catch trial incorrect
        attentionCheck != "Whether faces were real humans or computer-generated" ~ "exclude", #exclude if failed attention check
        rwm.acc.miss > 5 ~ "exclude", #exclude if >10% trials missing for any condition
        swm.acc.miss > 5 ~ "exclude",
        rwf.acc.miss > 5 ~ "exclude",
        swf.acc.miss > 5 ~ "exclude",
        rwm.conf.miss > 5 ~ "exclude",
        swm.conf.miss > 5 ~ "exclude",
        rwf.conf.miss > 5 ~ "exclude",
        swf.conf.miss > 5 ~ "exclude"
        )) 

#code reasons for exclusions
df.allPs <- df.allPs %>%
  rowwise() %>%
    mutate(excReason.tech = case_when(
      ResponseId == "R_1LjsyHjBrTnn6CG" ~ "self-reported tech error")) %>%
    mutate(excReason.incomplete = case_when(
      Progress < 98 ~ "incomplete")) %>%
    mutate(excReason.phone = case_when(
      str_detect(operateSys, "Android") ~ "used phone", operateSys == "iPhone" ~ "used phone")) %>% 
    mutate(excReason.white = case_when(
      confirmWhite != "Yes, my ethnicity is White/European/Caucasian" ~ "not White")) %>%
    mutate(excReason.notUS = case_when(
      USstate == "I do not reside in the United States" ~ "not living in US")) %>%
    mutate(excReason.yrsOutUS = case_when(
      yearsOutsideUS > 2 ~ ">2 yrs outside US pre-18")) %>%
    mutate(excReason.condFP = case_when(
      incNoCond != "No, none of these statements apply to me" ~ "condition affecting face processing",)) %>%
    mutate(excReason.catch = case_when(
      catch.acc < 4 ~ ">1 error on catch trials",)) %>%
    mutate(excReason.attCheck = case_when(
      attentionCheck != "Whether faces were real humans or computer-generated" ~ "failed attention check")) %>%
    mutate(excReason.miss = case_when(
      rwm.acc.miss > 5 ~ ">10% missing in 1 or more conditions",
      swm.acc.miss > 5 ~ ">10% missing in 1 or more conditions",
      rwf.acc.miss > 5 ~ ">10% missing in 1 or more conditions",
      swf.acc.miss > 5 ~ ">10% missing in 1 or more conditions",
      rwm.conf.miss > 5 ~ ">10% missing in 1 or more conditions",
      swm.conf.miss > 5 ~ ">10% missing in 1 or more conditions",
      rwf.conf.miss > 5 ~ ">10% missing in 1 or more conditions",
      swf.conf.miss > 5 ~ ">10% missing in 1 or more conditions"
  )) 

#concatenate reasons for exclusions into a single variable
df.allPs <- df.allPs %>%
  mutate(excReason = paste(excReason.incomplete, excReason.phone, excReason.white, excReason.notUS, excReason.yrsOutUS, excReason.condFP, excReason.catch, excReason.attCheck, excReason.miss, sep = "; ")) %>%
  mutate(excReason = gsub("NA; ", "", excReason)) %>%
  mutate(excReason = gsub("NA", "", excReason))

#generate dataset for included Ps
df.incPs <- df.allPs %>%
  filter(is.na(exclude))

#generate dataset for excluded Ps
df.excPs <- df.allPs %>%
  filter(exclude == "exclude") 

#save data
write.csv(df.incPs, paste("../data/LM_Expt1_includedPs.csv"))
write.csv(df.excPs, paste("../data/LM_Expt1_excludedPs.csv"))

#table showing Ns for male vs female Ps across conditions for included Ps
table(df.incPs$cond, df.incPs$gender)
x <- table(df.incPs$cond)
sum(x)

#cleanup: remove dfs that are no longer needed
rm(df.excPs)

```

# Compute scores

Here, we compute scores for each of the face types.

```{r, compute-scores}

#compute all scores 
df.incPs <- df.incPs %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  #compute total accuracy for CG vs human
    mutate(rwm.acc = rowSums(across(starts_with("rwm0") & ends_with(".acc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rwm.acc = case_when(str_detect(cond, "mc") ~ rwm.acc, str_detect(cond, "fc") ~ NA_real_)) %>%
    mutate(swm.acc = rowSums(across(starts_with("swm0") & ends_with(".acc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(swm.acc = case_when(str_detect(cond, "mc") ~ swm.acc, str_detect(cond, "fc") ~ NA_real_)) %>%
    mutate(rwf.acc = rowSums(across(starts_with("rwf0") & ends_with(".acc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rwf.acc = case_when(str_detect(cond, "fc") ~ rwf.acc, str_detect(cond, "mc") ~ NA_real_)) %>%
    mutate(swf.acc = rowSums(across(starts_with("swf0") & ends_with(".acc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(swf.acc = case_when(str_detect(cond, "fc") ~ swf.acc, str_detect(cond, "mc") ~ NA_real_)) %>%
    mutate(wm.acc = rowSums(across((starts_with("rwm0") & ends_with(".acc"))|(starts_with("swm0") & ends_with(".acc"))), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(wm.acc = case_when(str_detect(cond, "mc") ~ wm.acc, str_detect(cond, "fc") ~ NA_real_)) %>%
    mutate(wf.acc = rowSums(across((starts_with("rwf0") & ends_with(".acc"))|(starts_with("swf0") & ends_with(".acc"))), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(wf.acc = case_when(str_detect(cond, "fc") ~ wf.acc, str_detect(cond, "mc") ~ NA_real_)) %>%
  #compute pc accuracy for each condition/combination of conditions of interest
    mutate(rwm.accPc = (rwm.acc/50)*100) %>% 
    mutate(swm.accPc = (swm.acc/50)*100) %>%
    mutate(rwf.accPc = (rwf.acc/50)*100) %>% 
    mutate(swf.accPc = (swf.acc/50)*100) %>%
    mutate(wm.accPc = (wm.acc/100)*100) %>% 
    mutate(wf.accPc = (wf.acc/100)*100) %>%
  #compute percent human responses                
    mutate(rwf.HumPc = rwf.accPc, 
           swf.HumPc = 100-swf.accPc, 
           rwm.HumPc = rwm.accPc, 
           swm.HumPc = 100-swm.accPc) %>%
  #compute mean RT for each condition 
    mutate(rwm.RTacc = rowMeans(across(starts_with("rwm0") & ends_with(".submitacc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
    mutate(swm.RTacc = rowMeans(across(starts_with("swm0") & ends_with(".submitacc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rwf.RTacc = rowMeans(across(starts_with("rwf0") & ends_with(".submitacc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
    mutate(swf.RTacc = rowMeans(across(starts_with("swf0") & ends_with(".submitacc")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  #compute mean confidence ratings for each condition
    mutate(rwm.conf = rowMeans(across(starts_with("rwm0") & ends_with(".conf")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
    mutate(swm.conf = rowMeans(across(starts_with("swm0") & ends_with(".conf")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rwf.conf = rowMeans(across(starts_with("rwf0") & ends_with(".conf")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
    mutate(swf.conf = rowMeans(across(starts_with("swf0") & ends_with(".conf")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rw.conf = rowMeans(across(starts_with("rw") & contains("0") & ends_with(".conf")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
    mutate(sw.conf = rowMeans(across(starts_with("sw") & contains("0") & ends_with(".conf")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
    mutate(w.conf = rowMeans(across((starts_with("rw") | starts_with("sw")) & contains("0") & ends_with(".conf")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  #compute mean RT for confidence ratings for each condition
    mutate(rwm.RTconf = rowMeans(across(starts_with("rwm0") & ends_with(".submitconf")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
    mutate(swm.RTconf = rowMeans(across(starts_with("swm0") & ends_with(".submitconf")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rwf.RTconf = rowMeans(across(starts_with("rwf0") & ends_with(".submitconf")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
    mutate(swf.RTconf = rowMeans(across(starts_with("swf0") & ends_with(".submitconf")), na.rm = TRUE))

#replace NaN's with NA's
df.incPs[df.incPs == "NaN"] <- NA

#combine pc accuracy into single variable for each type of face (human or CG)
df.incPs$rw.accPc <- coalesce(df.incPs$rwm.accPc, df.incPs$rwf.accPc)
df.incPs$sw.accPc <- coalesce(df.incPs$swm.accPc, df.incPs$swf.accPc)
df.incPs$w.accPc <- coalesce(df.incPs$wm.accPc, df.incPs$wf.accPc)
df.incPs$rw.HumPc = df.incPs$rw.accPc 
df.incPs$sw.HumPc = 100-df.incPs$sw.accPc

#combine RTs into single variable for each type of face (human or CG)
df.incPs$rw.RTacc <- coalesce(df.incPs$rwf.RTacc, df.incPs$rwm.RTacc)
df.incPs$sw.RTacc <- coalesce(df.incPs$swf.RTacc, df.incPs$swm.RTacc)
df.incPs$rw.RTconf <- coalesce(df.incPs$rwf.RTconf, df.incPs$rwm.RTconf)
df.incPs$sw.RTconf <- coalesce(df.incPs$swf.RTconf, df.incPs$swm.RTconf)

```

Here, we compute our signal detection measures.

```{r, compute-sdt}

#from: https://www.r-bloggers.com/2018/03/compute-signal-detection-theory-indices-with-r/
#also see: https://people.brandeis.edu/~sekuler/stanislawTodorov1999.pdf

#compute misses by face gender and then combine into one variable
df.incPs$m.misses <- (100-df.incPs$rwm.accPc) #for male faces
df.incPs$f.misses <- (100-df.incPs$rwf.accPc) #for female faces
df.incPs$all.misses <- coalesce(df.incPs$m.misses, df.incPs$f.misses)

#compute FAs by face gender and then combine into one variable
df.incPs$m.FAs <- (100-df.incPs$swm.accPc) #for male faces
df.incPs$f.FAs <- (100-df.incPs$swf.accPc) #for female faces
df.incPs$all.FAs <- coalesce(df.incPs$m.FAs, df.incPs$f.FAs)

#compute SDT variables and combine into main df
sdt <- psycho::dprime(n_hit = df.incPs$rw.accPc, n_fa = df.incPs$all.FAs, n_miss = df.incPs$all.misses, n_cr = df.incPs$sw.accPc)
df.incPs <- cbind(df.incPs, sdt)

#save scored data
write.csv(df.incPs, paste("../data/LM_Expt1_includedPs_scored.csv"))

```

# Descriptives

Here, we get key descriptives for our selected sample.

```{r, describe, warning = FALSE}

#describe and view included data
descript.incPs <- describe(df.incPs)
view(descript.incPs)

#save descriptives
write.csv(descript.incPs, paste("../output/LM_Expt1_descriptives_includedPs.csv"))

```

# Test d prime, b, and c

Here, we compare dprime and c to 0 and b to 1.

```{r, sdt-analysis}

qqnorm(df.incPs$dprime)
qqline(df.incPs$dprime)
t.test(df.incPs$dprime, mu = 0)

qqnorm(df.incPs$beta)
qqline(df.incPs$beta)
t.test(df.incPs$beta, mu = 1) #bias > 1 = towards saying "yes" is human

qqnorm(df.incPs$c)
qqline(df.incPs$c)
t.test(df.incPs$c, mu = 0) #negative c = false alarms > misses

```

# Correlations

Here, we analyse correlations between key variables of interest.

```{r, correlations}

df.incPs.corrs <- df.incPs %>%
  select('rw.accPc', 'sw.accPc', 'w.accPc', 'rw.conf', 'sw.conf', 'w.conf', 'beta')

incPs.corrs <- corr.test(df.incPs.corrs, use = "pairwise", method = "pearson", adjust = "none", 
    alpha = .05, ci = TRUE, minlength = 5, normal = TRUE)

incPs.corrs$r %>%
  pander()
incPs.corrs$p %>%
  pander()

```

# Reshape wide data into long format

Here, we reshape our data into long format.

```{r, reshape-w2l}

#subset data
dfl.incPs <- df.incPs %>%
  select('ResponseId', 'rwm.accPc':'swf.accPc')

dfl.incPs <- dfl.incPs %>%  
  gather("var", "mean.accPc", c(rwm.accPc, swm.accPc, rwf.accPc, swf.accPc), convert = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(face.sex = substr(var, 3, 3)) %>%
  mutate(face.format = substr(var, 1, 1))

dfl.incPs$face.sex <- as.factor(dfl.incPs$face.sex)
dfl.incPs$face.format <- as.factor(dfl.incPs$face.format)
  
```

# ANOVA

Here, we test for differences in accuracy between human and CG
faces (by face sex),
following:<https://www.datanovia.com/en/lessons/mixed-anova-in-r/#three-way-bww-b>

```{r, ANOVA, warning = FALSE}

#check for outliers
dfl.incPs %>%
  group_by(face.sex, face.format) %>%
  identify_outliers(mean.accPc) #no outliers

#shapiro test for normality
dfl.incPs %>%
  group_by(face.sex, face.format) %>%
  shapiro_test(mean.accPc) #does not meet assumption of normality

#qqplots
ggqqplot(dfl.incPs, "mean.accPc", ggtheme = theme_bw()) +
  facet_grid(face.sex ~ face.format, labeller = "label_both") #visual = minor violations

#homogeneity of variance
dfl.incPs %>%
  group_by(face.sex) %>%
  levene_test(mean.accPc ~ face.format) #meets assumption of homogeneity of variance

#ANOVA
aov.res <- anova_test(
  data = dfl.incPs, dv = mean.accPc, wid = ResponseId,
  within = c(face.format), between = c(face.sex)
  )
aov.out <- as.data.frame(aov.res)
print(aov.out)

```

# Pairwise comparisons

Here, we include comparisons to chance.

```{r, t-tests}

#t-tests for CG vs human accuracy
t.test(df.incPs$swm.accPc, df.incPs$rwm.accPc, paired = TRUE) 
t.test(df.incPs$swf.accPc, df.incPs$rwf.accPc, paired = TRUE)
t.test(df.incPs$sw.accPc, df.incPs$rw.accPc, paired = TRUE)

#t-test for CG or human accuracy vs chance
t.test(df.incPs$rwf.accPc, mu = 50)
t.test(df.incPs$swf.accPc, mu = 50)
t.test(df.incPs$rwm.accPc, mu = 50)
t.test(df.incPs$swm.accPc, mu = 50)
t.test(df.incPs$rw.accPc, mu = 50)
t.test(df.incPs$sw.accPc, mu = 50)

#t-test for CG vs human confidence ratings
t.test(df.incPs$rw.conf, df.incPs$sw.conf, paired = TRUE)

```
